city-structure-zones.alt: A city model of five rings around one center, numbered 1 at the center to 5 at the outer edge. The rings are equal bands with no wedges. A lake lies along the east side, so the rings are drawn as half circles open to the lake. A railroad enters zone 2 from the west.

city-structure-models.alt: Four small diagrams. Concentric zone: rings around one downtown center. Sector: wedges that run out from the center along transport lines. Multiple nuclei: several separate centers scattered in the city, such as a downtown, an airport area, a university and an industrial park. Galactic city: an old downtown plus edge cities spaced along a ring highway, with homes and farmland between.

city-structure-latin-american.alt: A half-circle city around a central business district by a main plaza. A narrow wedge, the spine, runs from the center along a grand avenue: wealthy homes, offices and parks, ending at a mall and a wealthy suburb. Around the center lie rings: first older, solid homes; then homes being improved bit by bit; then on the outer edge self-built squatter settlements. Factories sit in another wedge along a rail line.
